reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Thin cap plus large lipid core plus inflammation means vulnerable plaque
Most myocardial infarctions arise from rupture of previously non severe plaques
Infrarenal abdominal aneurysm rupture risk climbs with diameter
Dissection is medial splitting, not simple dilation
reference.pathophysiology: Retained oxidised LDL drives intimal inflammation where macrophages, T cells and smooth muscle cells build and remodel plaque. Matrix degrading enzymes from macrophages thin the fibrous cap while necrotic cores expand, until mechanical stress ruptures the cap and thrombosis follows. Medial degeneration from hypertension, atherosclerosis or connective tissue defects weakens the aorta toward aneurysm or dissection.
additionalDifferentials: True versus false aneurysm versus dissection
additionalInvestigations: Ultrasound diameter surveillance for abdominal aneurysm
CT angiography for dissection and rupture assessment
Lipid profile and global risk scoring for prevention
